events.fact: Webflow OAuth authorization endpoint is https://webflow.com/oauth/authorize and token exchange endpoint is POST https://api.webflow.com/oauth/access_token.
To register an OAuth app in Webflow, navigate to Workspace settings, select Apps & Integrations, create a new app under the App Development section, and choose the 'Data Client' building block.
Only workspace administrators are authorized to view a client secret in Webflow.
Webflow authorization codes expire in 15 minutes and can only be used once.
Webflow API rate limits depend on plan: Starter and Basic plans get 60 RPM, CMS, eCommerce, and Business plans get 120 RPM, and Enterprise has custom limits.

events.fact: Webflow OAuth authorization codes expire in 15 minutes, and access tokens can be revoked via POST to https://webflow.com/oauth/revoke_authorization.
Before marketplace publication, Webflow restricts custom apps to the developer's own workspace by default, with an option to request up to 5 test user accounts via Webflow support.
Private apps in Webflow are intended for specific workspaces or custom implementations without public marketplace listing, but they still require submitting through the standard review process.
Webflow offers a free Developer Workspace plan for building and testing integrations, while site hosting plans are billed separately.
